minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard its state legislators on Chapter 70, police training, ARPA and buildings; no budget vote taken.
minutes.summary: The committee hosted its three state legislators to discuss Chapter 70 and the Student Opportunity Act, ARPA flexibility, police reform training costs, records retention, 40B and town buildings. The town manager previewed legislative earmark priorities and gave a finance update. Four sets of minutes were approved, and the chair said the building committee representative question must be decided at the next meeting.

public_comment.topic: Thanked the committee for inviting legislators; said the Student Opportunity Act limits Chapter 70 growth for small suburban towns.
Urged school bus contract language so the town does not pay for undelivered service, and urged prioritizing among the many issues facing the town.

votes.motion: Approve four sets of minutes (Oct 28, Nov 4, Nov 16, Dec 9).

budget_items.what_was_said: Town manager listed last year's requests and the FY23 priorities: culvert, old primary school abatement, 925 Mass Ave, senior center.
Town manager said the final Treasury rule lets lost revenue be used broadly, widening ARPA uses.
A legislator said the police chief estimated training costs for reserve officers for the current year and three-year total.
A legislator noted a base budget with the town contributing the larger share beyond state aid.
Chair said town policy caps debt service at a share of the levy.

Chair set next meeting as the deadline to decide the building design committee representative.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee took no budget vote and heard its three state legislators on Chapter 70, police training costs, ARPA, buildings and 40B.
The town manager previewed FY23 legislative earmark priorities: a culvert, old primary school abatement, 925 Mass Ave and the senior center.
The town manager said the final Treasury rule lets ARPA lost revenue be used broadly, widening what the money can pay for.
The chair set the next meeting as the deadline to decide who represents the committee on the municipal building design committee.
The committee skipped Feb 10, set Feb 17 and Feb 24, and set Jan 27 for the five-year forecast and capital plan.

why_it_matters: State aid formulas such as Chapter 70 and the Student Opportunity Act help set how much of the school budget falls on local taxes, and the committee raised them with the people who can change them.
The earmark list, ARPA flexibility and the building committee seat bear on what the town builds and how it pays for it, and the Jan 27 forecast and capital plan will frame the coming budget.
watch_next: Next meeting: the committee's decision on its representative to the municipal building design committee.
Jan 27: the five-year forecast and capital plan, before the Feb 17 and Feb 24 meetings.
